How to Reduce BIM Coordination Rework

Most coordination rework comes from process, not software. Ten practical changes that reduce it.

Coordination rework, the same clashes coming back cycle after cycle and models remodelled after late decisions, is rarely caused by the software. It comes from the process around it. These are the changes that make the biggest difference.

Set up correctly once

  1. Shared coordinates from day one. Misaligned models create false clashes and hide real ones.
  2. Agreed zones and levels. Split the building into zones that every discipline uses, so clash runs and responsibilities line up.
  3. Clearance rules in writing. Agree insulation, access and maintenance clearances before modelling, not after the first clash report.

Run clash cycles with priorities

  1. Coordinate in order. Structure first, then gravity drainage, then large ductwork, then pressurised pipework and cable containment.
  2. Group clashes. One duct crossing twenty beams is one problem, not twenty. Group by element and zone before assigning.
  3. Assign an owner and a date. Every clash group needs a responsible party and a target cycle.

Make decisions stick

  1. Keep a decision log. Record what was agreed in each coordination meeting and who changes what. Undocumented decisions are the main source of repeat clashes.
  2. Freeze what is resolved. Mark coordinated zones and control changes to them.

Check before sharing

  1. Model QA before every issue. A checklist from the BEP catches naming, LOD and coordinate problems before they reach the federated model.
  2. Measure the trend. Track open clash groups by cycle; if the number is not falling, the process needs attention, not more clash runs.
